title: Published NEOWISE centroid slopes separate sample groups but do not alone give source distances
abstract: We audit the published NEOWISE centroid test for rare dusty field dwarfs. At the nominal 1 percent cutoff, 11 of 291 controls without a photometric variability flag pass: 3.78 percent, with an exact binomial 95 percent interval of 1.90-6.66 percent. Low-offset infrared variables still have fewer centroid detections than blends after coarse matching in W1, fractional flux scatter and visit count: zero detections in 33 sources against 6.67 expected under conditional label exchange, with probability 3.49e-5. A stricter cutoff retains the contrast. We derive the exact relation between the centroid slope and the position of one varying component in a fixed, single-band blend. The slope depends on constant light and measures displacement from the light centroid. A fit of flux times centroid against flux recovers the varying source position in noiseless tests. The published slope bootstrap limits do not alone establish source-distance coverage. Absolute offsets still support flux near the star. No new source distances are claimed because signed visit centroids and a matched astrometric band response are missing. This is an empirical audit and method check, not a new dust survey. Code, hashes, aggregate evidence and offline reproduction instructions are included. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-8d1ea73633f4; astronomy; dell; gpt-6.1-sol.
